discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (moiré quantum matter)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional materials and moiré superlattices
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene layers to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands nearly flat, so that Coulomb interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers realized this with precise tear-and-stack fabrication. They found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity that can be switched on with a gate voltage. Together these works created moiré quantum matter: a platform where twist angle, stacking and electrostatic gating control band structure and interactions in a single device. Hundreds of groups worldwide have since used it to observe Mott and generalized Wigner crystals, orbital ferromagnetism, and integer and fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in graphene and transition-metal-dichalcogenide moiré systems. Theory and experiment together have given physicists a fundamentally new, tunable way to create and study strongly correlated and topological electronic states.
